msItem.title: Expositio omeliarum dominicalium (sermons by G. Peraldus, ascribed s. xvi to N. Waterton (= Aquavilla)
msItem.note: Mr John de Stok' was instituted to Twyford, Bucks. in 1241 (Rot. Rob. Grosseteste, p. 359). A Mr John de Stok' bought Royal MS. 8 A VIII at Hoxne Suffolk in 1246.

provenance.p: Hunc librum contulat [sic] magister Iohannes de Stok' presbiter et rector ecclesiarum de Twyford et Hunede pro salute anime sue et omnium parochianorum suorum deo et beate marie et communitati fratrum predicatorum Subbirie commorantium: qui fraudulenter quocunque genere alienacionis a dicta communitate alienaverit vel scripturam istam quocumque tempore maliciose preter suam conscientiam deleverit ipso facto anathema est maranata, salvo tamen Iohanni de Hundene sacerdoti et dicto I. si velit usu dicti libri suo dumtaxat perpetuo. Actum a. d. mᵒ ccᵒ lᵒ sexto duodecimo Kal. marcii (fol. 227v). Inscription erased at foot of fol. 1r.

history.provenance:
Melbourne, Derbyshire. Parish churchIste liber datum Iohanni Reed vicario de Melburn et successoribus suis in ecclesia beate marie imperpetuum per venerabilem presbiterum dominum Iohannem Bredone quondam vicarium de Bredon A.D. 1514. Ita quod semper erit in custodia vicarii de Melburn ibidem residentis (fol. ii).
A note on the index card records that the church at Melbourne (Derbyshire), a few miles from Breedon (Leicestershire) is dedicated to St Michael.

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).

revisionDesc.change: Melbourne provenance added. Transcribed from corresponding index card in Neil R. Ker, et al., ‘Medieval Libraries of Great Britain’, index, Oxford, 1937–2025 (held at Oxford, Bodleian Library).
